summary: Add an offline-only local game session endpoint and browser frame bridge for Snake and Maze Chase, using the pinned WLED AsyncWebServer and existing Matrix-to-AUX renderer.

findings.statement: Pinned WLED DDP handling routes realtime pixel data through setRealtimePixel, outside the project canonical Matrix frame consumed by its AUX projection.
The project already contains deterministic JavaScript Snake and Maze Chase engines and a canonical Matrix-to-AUX renderer.

findings.statement: Keeping game logic in the existing browser-side JavaScript and sending bounded RGB565 frames to the existing local firmware server minimizes duplicated game logic while preserving the canonical renderer path.

native_capability_check.capability: Pinned WLED local AsyncWebServer, JSON handlers, Matrix usermod and canonical Matrix/AUX frame renderer.
native_capability_check.rationale: Native DDP/WebSocket pixel streaming has no session-bound owner/guest input authorization and bypasses the project canonical Matrix-to-AUX game frame. Existing server and renderer are reused, but a game-scoped endpoint/frame adapter is necessary.

alternatives.compatibility: Does not enter HBNF session authorization or canonical Matrix-to-AUX output path.

alternatives.maintenance: Would require maintaining duplicate engines and conformance tests.

alternatives.name: Browser JS game logic with bounded local session/frame adapter
alternatives.maturity: Uses existing project engines and WLED server/renderer; adapter is bespoke glue.
alternatives.maintenance: One small adapter; no duplicated game engines or new runtime package.
alternatives.compatibility: Uses existing local Wi-Fi, 32x16 Matrix and canonical Matrix/AUX renderer.
alternatives.provenance: Existing HBNF deterministic JS runtimes and canonical Matrix/AUX renderer
alternatives.license: Existing project code; no added package.
alternatives.documentation_support: Existing project source, pinned WLED handler APIs, and focused host checks.
alternatives.rationale: Smallest viable path meeting local phone input, session-bound actions, and shared Matrix/AUX frame output.

decision_rationale.selected_path: Browser-side existing JS engines send authenticated bounded 32x16 RGB565 frames to a local game endpoint in the Matrix usermod; that endpoint feeds the existing canonical Matrix frame, then AUX projection.
decision_rationale.challenger_analysis: Native WLED realtime pixel paths bypass the session authorization and canonical Matrix/AUX bridge. Porting engines to ESP32 duplicates logic and tests. The selected adapter still cannot provide global WLED API isolation or confidentiality on plain HTTP, so claims stay scoped to game endpoint and physical use is unverified.
decision_rationale.tradeoffs: Adds one firmware endpoint and generated PROGMEM browser assets; frame transport is about 10 KiB/s at 10 fps. It adds no external dependency. Plain HTTP exposes credentials to same-LAN observers and other WLED APIs remain separate.
decision_rationale.simplest_robust_solution: Reuse the pinned AsyncWebServer, existing game engines, and canonical renderer with fixed-size RGB565 frames and explicit session checks.
decision_rationale.critical_path_reason: Both games need one shared authenticated phone-input-to-renderer path; this adapter is the smallest reusable integration.
alternatives_considered: Native WLED DDP/WebSocket realtime pixel stream
Browser-side JS engines plus local authenticated frame endpoint

bespoke_exception.unmet_requirement: Secure local phone/iPad play of Snake and Maze Chase with 32x16 Matrix rendering and shared AUX output, offline and without a development computer.
bespoke_exception.why_minimal_glue_is_insufficient: Native WLED DDP/WebSocket does not bind frame writes to this project game-session owner/guest permissions and bypasses the canonical Matrix/AUX output path.
bespoke_exception.required_custom_scope: Session-bound game commands, random per-session owner/guest tokens and controller IDs, input sequence checks, guest direction-only permissions, fixed frame size/rate, timeout and owner revocation, plus bridge to existing renderer.
bespoke_exception.maintenance_burden: Small source adapter and asset generator; existing JS game logic remains the single source; no new dependency.
bespoke_exception.technical_debt_implications: Plain HTTP exposes game credentials to same-LAN observers; other WLED endpoints are outside this game-specific authorization; physical performance and coexistence remain unverified.
bespoke_exception.test_plan: Focused native C++ session tests; JS controller/runtime and source wiring tests; generated asset parity; pinned ESP32 firmware compile and OTA slot check; supervised hardware validation still required.
bespoke_exception.rollback_exit_path: Keep installed baseline unchanged; remove arcade routes/assets/link and revert source commit.
